patch.value: Platform nightly legs fail on half of all days and nothing measures the rate: each alert opens a fresh issue and closes on repair, so a 28-occurrence family reads as 28 first occurrences

Measured 2026-08-03 against the live GitHub Actions record and the tracker itself.

The scheduled Nightly Validation workflow has raised 28 failure alerts between 2026-06-20 and 2026-08-03. That is 23 distinct calendar days carrying at least one red leg across a 44-day window, so a platform leg fails on roughly half of all days. By leg: windows-latest Node 24 nineteen times, macos-latest Node 24 six times, ubuntu-latest three times. Every one of the 28 alerts is closed. Median time from alert to closure is 5.7 hours and the maximum is 175 hours.

The alerting itself works exactly as specified. The workflow searches for an open issue with the same title, comments on it if one exists, and otherwise opens a new one. Because each occurrence is repaired within hours, the search never finds an open issue, so every occurrence opens a fresh one. The channel therefore encodes each failure as a first occurrence and destroys the recurrence count as a side effect of working correctly.

The tracker shows the same shape. A title census over all items returns roughly thirty closed items whose subject is a platform nightly regression, spanning at least eight months of releases and many independent root causes: POSIX path literals, realpath canonicalization asymmetry, short-name temp directories, native path quoting, errno literals, spawn and lock behaviour, and most recently a workspace slug encoding. Each was diagnosed, fixed, closed and forgotten. No item, report, gate or command anywhere computes the family rate.

The consequence is a decision error, not a test error. Every individual repair looks proportionate because it is judged against one failing spec. The correct comparison is against the family: a defect class that recurs on half of all days with a median five-hour repair is consuming more sustained effort than the pre-merge control it lacks would cost, and nothing in the project can state that sentence with evidence. The exact same argument was already accepted for the release pipeline, where the failure rate of the scheduled auto-release was made a first-class defect precisely because the recovery path closes its own evidence. This item is that argument applied to the platform legs.

Scope is measurement and escalation, not the repair of any individual leg and not the choice of which checks run before merge. It must produce a durable, queryable rate per leg per period, a recurrence identity that survives repair, and a declared threshold that changes behaviour when crossed.

A durable per-leg failure-rate report is derivable from recorded data alone and states occurrences, distinct affected days, and repair latency over a caller-chosen window; The alert channel carries a stable recurrence identity so a repaired occurrence does not reset the count, and the identity survives closure of the alert and of the tracking item; A declared threshold on the rate changes behaviour rather than only reporting, and the behaviour change is recorded where the release decision can read it; The historical 28 occurrences and the tracker items that repaired them are reconciled into one queryable family with no hand-maintained list; A negative control proves the meter reports zero on a period with no failures rather than failing open

value.text:
A clean natural experiment, observed 2026-08-03 immediately after this item was filed.

A commit touching only tracker data under the pm store, with no source, script, workflow or test file changed, turned the Windows regression job on main red. Two tests in the init command suite failed at 30010 and 30002 milliseconds, which is the generic Vitest timeout rather than an assertion. Re-running the failed job against byte-identical content passed, and main is green at the same commit.

The experiment is clean because the input could not have caused a behavioural change. Tracker data is not read by that suite, which sandboxes its own store path. So the failure carried zero information about the commit and the leg still reported red.

Two consequences for this item.

First, the measured failure rate is a mixture and nothing separates its parts. Of the 28 alerts counted here, an unknown fraction are product defects that a pre-merge control would have caught, and an unknown fraction are infrastructure timeouts that no control can catch because there is nothing to catch. A rate that mixes them cannot justify any decision, which strengthens rather than weakens the case for measuring it properly: the first thing the meter has to do is partition.

Second, the timeout class is itself a recurrence. Two items in this tracker are already closed for the same subject, Windows init package acceptance exceeding the generic Vitest timeout, and both closed with a per-site timeout increase. The class has returned on a third site. That is the second independent recurrence found today and it arrived, unprompted, in the CI response to the commit that filed the recurrence work.

Partitioning rule this suggests, recorded as input rather than as a decision: a failure whose signature is a timeout at the declared limit, on a leg whose median passing duration for that suite is far below the limit, and which passes on re-run with identical content, is infrastructure. Everything else is a candidate defect until proved otherwise. The re-run is the discriminator and it is cheap.
